reasons: query1 PromQL multiplies the rate by a constant `100 *` that does not appear in the Datadog source; numeric constants not in the source are not allowed, so the expression must be dropped.

postgresql.tup_inserted, tup_deleted and tup_updated are monotonic sums counting rows inserted, deleted and updated, so they match the Datadog rows_* counters; rate() over $__rate_interval is valid for these sums.
Template variable $scope has no prefix and default '*', so dropping it is correct; avg() across series matches the default Datadog aggregation with no by-clause.
Outcome translated is appropriate since an exact OTel mapping exists; the blocking defect is only the injected constant in query1.
